verses.text: Then Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He called the elders, leaders, judges and officers of Israel, and they came and stood before God.

Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, including Terah, the father of Abraham and Nahor. They worshipped other gods.
But I took your father Abraham from the land beyond the river and led him all through Canaan. I gave him many descendants. I gave him Isaac,
and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Seir as his own, but Jacob and his family went down to Egypt.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with the plagues I did there. After that I brought you out.
When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, you came to the sea. The Egyptians chased them with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.

But they cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. You saw with your own eyes what I did to Egypt. Then you lived in the desert for a long time.
I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hands. I destroyed them ahead of you, and you took their land.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, got ready to fight against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam, so he blessed you again and again, and I saved you from Balak.

Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites and Jebusites. But I gave them into your hands.
I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out, including the two Amorite kings. You did not do it with your own sword or bow.
I gave you land you had not worked for and cities you had not built, and now you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant.'
So now, honour the LORD and serve him with all your heart and truly. Throw away the gods your ancestors worshipped beyond the Euphrates River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

But if serving the LORD seems wrong to you, then choose today whom you will serve: the gods your ancestors served beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you are living. But as for me and my family, we will serve the LORD."
The people answered, "We would never leave the LORD to serve other gods!

It was the LORD our God who brought us and our parents up out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. He did those great miracles in front of our eyes. He protected us on our whole journey and among all the nations we passed through.
The LORD drove out all the nations ahead of us, including the Amorites who lived in this land. We too will serve the LORD, because he is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You are not able to serve the LORD. He is a holy God. He is a jealous God, and he will not ignore your rebellion and your sins.
If you leave the LORD and serve foreign gods, he will turn against you and bring trouble on you and destroy you, even after he has been good to you."
But the people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."
Then Joshua said, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen to serve the LORD." "Yes, we are witnesses," they answered.
"Then throw away the foreign gods that are among you," said Joshua, "and give your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."
The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God and obey him."
That day at Shechem, Joshua made a covenant for the people, and he gave them rules and laws.
Joshua wrote these things in the book of the law of God. Then he took a large stone and set it up under the big oak tree near the holy place of the LORD.
He said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a witness against us. It has heard everything the LORD said to us. It will be a witness against you if you are unfaithful to your God."
Then Joshua sent the people away, each to their own land.
After this, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of a hundred and ten.
They buried him on his own land at Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD all the time Joshua was alive, and all the time of the elders who lived after him and had seen everything the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, were buried at Shechem, in the piece of land Jacob had bought for a hundred silver coins from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem. This land belonged to Joseph's descendants.
And Eleazar son of Aaron died. He was buried at Gibeah, the hill that had been given to his son Phinehas in the hill country of Ephraim.
